english.note: This is the all-purpose everyday adjective for feeling or showing anger.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone is angry or annoyed.
Use 嬲 as the all-purpose choice when someone is angry, distressed, or unhappy.
Use this as the all-purpose choice when someone is irritated or angry with a person or situation.
Use this for a person who is irritated or angry, where English “salty” describes an upset attitude rather than food.
Use this for being annoyed or angry, rather than for physical bending or determination.

examples.english: They are so angry that they refuse to talk to me.
examples.jyutping: keoi5 nau1 dou3 m4 hang2 tung4 ngo5 gong2 je5
ngo5 zan1 hai6 hou2 nau1 nei5

examples.english: I'm really upset and don't want to talk to him.
examples.traditional: 我真係嬲，唔想同佢講嘢。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 nau1 m4 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 gong2 je5

examples.english: I’m really annoyed that you did this.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 nau1 nei5 gam2 joeng2 zou6

examples.english: He was so salty after losing the game; he is really petty.
examples.traditional: 佢輸咗場波仲咁嬲，真係小器。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 syu1 zo2 coeng4 bo1 zung6 gam3 nau1 zan1 hai6 siu2 hei3

examples.english: You do not need to be bent out of shape; I did not mean it.
examples.traditional: 你唔使嬲，我唔係有心㗎。
examples.jyutping: nei5 m4 sai2 nau1 ngo5 m4 hai6 jau5 sam1 gaa3
